cost: PAU GASOL '04 IS DECLINED — target rimprot 78 ±2, reads 88, unchanged. He is not high because of votes (drep 0.00) or because of height: he sits EXACTLY on the recal_53 no-vote ceiling of 88, which overrides his composite, the Prot percentile and every weight above it. The only lever that can move him is the cap itself, and the cap IS an anchor set — recal_53 pinned Shawn Bradley '95, Shaquille O'Neal '93, Sam Bowie '85, DeSagana Diop '06 and Yao Ming '09 at 88 ±1 to record it. MEASURED, not argued: 120 reshapings were run offline (block/height reweighting 0.55-1.00, the Prot map A in 0.10-0.55 and B in 0.47-1.70, and a block-evidence-graded cap over four floors x 20 ramps). Gasol reads 88 in EVERY member of the first family — the cap does not care what the composite says. The best member of the second family reaches 80 (the band edge) and costs three anchors: Bobby Jones '82 96 -> 93, Joel Embiid '23 91 -> 88, Yao Ming '09 88 -> 86. The binding pair is Gasol '04 (block rate at the 89.5th percentile of 2004) against Yao Ming '09 (93.9th) — 4.4 percentile points that the two rulings ask to carry 10 card points, with Yao's own anchor on the other side. Tomer decides: either recal_53's cap set is re-opened, or Gasol stays at 88.

THE RELIABILITY ARGUMENT, which is the round's whole case for the first term. A season's defended-FG% differential is an ESTIMATE. On our own file, the same player's next season correlates at r = 0.345 for the 6ft+ series and 0.355 for Overall — so roughly two thirds of any season's deviation from neutral is noise. recal_86 read the raw diff as if it were the truth, which is why one tracked season could buy or cost twenty points. Regressing the diff by its reliability is the textbook correction and it is symmetric: the same line that takes 20 points off Isaiah Thomas '16 gives 11 back to J.J. Barea '18 and Tyler Ulis '18, who were being punished just as hard for one bad tracked year.

THE MIRROR ALREADY IN THE FILE: rimprot reads the rim series (r = 0.558, the most repeatable of the four) at a blend weight of 0.35. perdef was reading the LEAST repeatable half of the same measurement at 0.70. The round does not touch either weight — it fixes the value the weight is applied to.

WHY THE FLOOR HAD TO GO WITH IT. recal_86's own comment records that its absolute line and the r16 ladder land within 0.5-1.0 card points of each other. Once the branch became absolute the ladder was the same reading taken a second time with every discount switched off, and it OVERRODE the discounted one. 539 cards were sitting on it. Retiring it is one line (DFG_FLOORS = ()) and one line to restore.

THE NO-VOTE TRACKED BAND, before and after: 2,560 no-vote tracked cards, of which 108 read 60+ and the ceiling was Jason Terry '17 at 69 — Jason Terry, Mario Chalmers, Jeremy Lamb, Alec Burks, Devin Harris and Patrick Patterson, all lifted 17-24 points above their composites by one tracked season. That cohort, not Mitchell alone, is what his ruling names.

RIMPROT: WHERE THE VOTE ACTUALLY ENTERS. Two places, and the provenance row shows neither clearly. (1) ID += 0.25 * drep * height_pctile, an ADDITIVE lift worth +0.176 to McHale '88 — it took his blocks-and-height composite from 0.779 to 0.955. (2) recal_53's voted ceiling: with drep 1.00 his _w53 was 1.00, so the 88 cap simply did not apply. His diagnosis is right — the vote is doing the work. The drep and dbpm entries in the idc provenance row are display-only leftovers; recal_81 did remove DBPM from the composite.

WHY THE FIX IS THE CEILING AND NOT THE LIFT. Cutting the additive lift was measured at five settings (0.0, 0.10, and evidence ramps at 0.30/0.40/0.50/0.60/0.75). Every one of them deflates the ID pool, and Prot is a WITHIN-SEASON PERCENTILE, so the whole board renormalises: Tim Duncan '03 rose 98 -> 99 and Ben Wallace '04 fell 98 -> 97 at every setting, breaking two tol-0 anchors before McHale had moved far enough. Gating recal_53's unlock instead leaves the pool untouched — 77 cards move, all down, none by more than 8, and every rimprot anchor holds.

THE KNIFE EDGE, stated honestly. Bobby Jones '82 (blk 3.0%, 90th pctile, drep 1.00, 6'9") is McHale '88's twin, and Bobby Jones '81 (blk 2.0%, 78th pctile, drep 1.00) is a STRICTLY WEAKER card than McHale '88 on the axis the gate reads while supplying 20% of Jones '82's smoothed value. So the band is tight by necessity: 0.80 -> 0.86 puts McHale at 91 and holds Jones at 95; widening it to 0.90 takes Jones to 94 and breaks his recal_82 anchor. 91 is the lowest McHale can go while Bobby Jones stands, and it is inside the ruling's 86-92.

RIMPROT COLLATERAL, one sentence: 77 cards move, all down, and Kevin Garnett owns most of them — 12 All-Defensive selections on block rates between the 74th and 90th percentile, 99 -> 93 at his peak. He is the class the ruling describes, and his DEF is unchanged (96) because perdef, not rimprot, is where his defence was always paid.

PERDEF COLLATERAL: 2,614 cards move, almost exactly balanced (1,299 up, 1,315 down), 1,161 by 5+ — a big footprint because 539 cards were sitting on a floor and every tracked card since 2014 had its diff read raw. The top 12 is IDENTICAL, name for name and value for value: nothing at the summit is tracked-branch dependent.

DOWNSTREAM, which this agent does not own: d_ovr moves on 2,458 cards (463 by 10+), ovr on 1,937 (16 by 10+), o_ovr on none. Ajay Mitchell '26 DEF 75 -> 63, OVR 70 -> 63. Kevin McHale '88 DEF 93 -> 90, OVR 87 -> 86.

GASOL, THE MEASUREMENT BEHIND THE DECLINE. blk 3.9% = 89.5th percentile of 2004, height 7'0" = 93.2nd, drep 0.00. Composite ID 0.907, uncapped ID2 0.926 (card 92), capped to 0.888 -> 88. To put him at 78 the cap must fall to 0.786 for him and stay at 0.888 for Yao Ming '09, whose only separation from him is 4.4 percentile points of block rate and six inches of height. Every family tried is listed in COST. This is the recal_82 situation exactly: the number is reachable, the price is somebody else's ruling.

WHY THE THREE RULINGS ARE NOT ONE PROBLEM. McHale '88 is a VOTE story (drep 1.00, blk at the 81st percentile — the vote both added +0.176 of raw deterrence and switched the 88 cap off). Gasol '04 is a CAP story (drep 0.00 — he IS the cap, and nothing below a cap can be seen through it). They share the rimprot attribute and share no mechanism, which is why one lands and one does not.
